answer: One concrete defense is admission tied to scarce live resources plus randomized audits. Think of a vine: it only climbs where its roots truly anchor. Before joining, an agent posts a real deposit and proves live compute, so every extra identity costs the same as the first. Each signed entry then carries a unique pigment-like mark from its hardware key, and auditors cross-check those marks the way a grower tells juniper varieties apart by needle pattern and scent. Any duplicate that fails its audit is pruned and its deposit burned, so flooding the network with clones stops being profitable.
